newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke denies interest rate split with BoE.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke denies interest rate split with BoE.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke on Sunday denied any major policy disagreement with Bank of England Governor Eddie George and claimed a partnership with George that had kept inflation down.
In an interview with the BBC, Clarke parried questions about an independent central bank and said the key was that interest rate policy should be set to prevent rising prices.

His comments came after a call last week from George for a "modest pre-emptive" rate rise, though Clarke decided to leave rates unchanged at his monthly meeting with George on January 15 -- saying the strong pound was "very anti-inflationary."
Clarke has been accused of rejecting a rate rise in order to allow consumer confidence to improve ahead of an election that must be held by May.

"I'm not going around thinking I'm infallible," Clarke said. "The differences between us (himself and George) have not been enormous...there has been a perfectly sensible discussion about how to keep inflation down."
"The key is to go for low inflation," he said. "Between us we have achieved the best inflation record for 50 years."
